stem: Points \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) lie on the circle with center \(O\) shown. The measure of angle \(ACB\) is \(70^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(OAB\)?
solution: Central angle \(AOB\) intercepts the same arc as inscribed angle \(ACB\), so \(m\angle AOB = 2(70) = 140^{\circ}\).
\(OA = OB\) (radii), so triangle \(OAB\) is isosceles and its base angles are equal: \(m\angle OAB = \frac{180 - 140}{2} = 20^{\circ}\).

explanation.A: Correct. \(m\angle AOB = 140^{\circ}\), and the base angles of isosceles triangle \(OAB\) are each \(\frac{180 - 140}{2} = 20^{\circ}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(180 - 140 = 40\) is the sum of the two base angles; it still has to be split between angles \(OAB\) and \(OBA\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(\frac{180 - 70}{2} = 55\) treats the central angle as \(70^{\circ}\); the central angle is twice the inscribed angle.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Angle \(OAB\) is not equal to the inscribed angle \(ACB\).

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert all(abs(d('O',q)-6)<0.01 for q in 'ABC') and abs(ang('A','C','B')-70)<0.1
central=2*70
ans=Rational(180-central,2)
assert central==140 and ans==20 and abs(ang('A','O','B')-central)<0.1 and abs(ang('O','A','B')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
assert value(choices['B'])==180-central and value(choices['C'])==Rational(180-70,2)
